title: Why single out the Jews?
source_text: Συγγένειαν παρὰ πολλοῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν νομίζων εἶναι ὁ Κέλσος τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου πάντα μὲν ὀνομάζει τὰ ἔθνη ὡς ἀρξάμενα τοῦ τοιοῦδε δόγματος· οὐκ οἶδα δ᾿ ὅπως μόνους Ἰουδαίους συκοφαντεῖ, οὐ συγκαταλέγων αὐτῶν τὸ ἔθνος τοῖς λοιποῖς, ὡς εἴτε συμφιλοπονῆσαν ἐκείνοις καὶ ὁμοφρονῆσαν εἴτε παραπλήσια ἐν πολλοῖς δογματίσαν. ἄξιον οὖν αὐτὸν ἐρέσθαι, τί δήποτε ἱστορίαις μὲν βαρβάρων καὶ Ἑλλήνων πεπίστευκε περὶ τῆς ἀρχαιότητος ὧν ὠνόμασε, μόνου δὲ τοῦ ἔθνους τὰς ἱστορίας τούτου ψευδοποιεῖ. εἰ γὰρ ἕκαστοι τὰ παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἐξέθεντο φιλαλήθως, τί τοῖς Ἰουδαίων ἀπιστοῦμεν μόνοις προφήταις; εἰ δὲ κεχαρισμένως Μω(??)υσῆς καὶ οἱ προφῆται τῷ ἑαυτῶν λόγῳ πολλὰ ἀνέγραψαν περὶ τῶν παρὰ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς, διὰ τί τὸ παραπλήσιον οὐκ ἐροῦμεν καὶ περὶ τῶν ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσι συγγραφέων; ἢ Αἰγύπτιοι μὲν ἐν ταῖς ἑαυτῶν ἱστορίαις Ἰουδαίους κακολογοῦντες πιστοί εἰσι περὶ Ἰουδαίων· ταὐτὰ δὲ λέγοντες Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ Αἰγυπτίων, πολλὰ ἀδίκως πεπονθέναι ἀναγράφοντες ἑαυτοὺς καὶ διὰ τοῦτο λέγοντες αὐτοὺς κεκολάσθαι ὑπὸ θεοῦ, ψεύδονται; καὶ οὐ περὶ Αἰγυπτίων γε μόνων τοῦτο λεκτέον· εὑρήσομεν γὰρ ἐπιπλοκὴν Ἀσσυρίων πρὸς Ἰουδαίους, καὶ ταῦτα ἱστορούμενα ἐν ταῖς Ἀσσυρίων ἀρχαιολογίαις. οὕτω δὲ καὶ Ἀσσυρίους ἀνέγραψαν ἑαυτοῖς πολεμίους οἱ Ἰουδαίων συγγραφεῖς, ἵνα μὴ δόξω προλαμβάνων λέγειν τὸ οἱ προφῆται. ὅρα οὖν εὐθέως τὸ φίλαυτον τοῦ τοῖσδε μέν τισι πιστεύοντος ὡς σοφοῖς ἔθνεσι τῶνδε δὲ καταγινώσκοντος ὡς πάντῃ ἀνοήτων. ἄκουε γὰρ λέγοντος τοῦ Κέλσου ὅτι ἔστιν ἀρχαῖος ἄνωθεν λόγος, περὶ ὃν δὴ ἀεὶ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὰ σοφώτατα καὶ πόλεις καὶ ἄνδρες σοφοὶ κατεγένοντο. καὶ οὐκ ἐβουλήθη ἔθνος σοφώτατον εἰπεῖν κἂν παραπλησίως [καὶ] Αἰγυπτίοις καὶ Ἀσσυρίοις καὶ Ἰνδοῖς καὶ Πέρσαις καὶ Ὀδρύσαις καὶ Σαμόθρᾳξι καὶ Ἐλευσινίοις τοὺς Ἰουδαίους.
pass_a_gloss: Kinship (συγγένεια) among many of the nations thinking there to be of the same doctrine (λόγος), Celsus names all the nations as having begun (ἄρχομαι) such a dogma (δόγμα); I do not know how he slanders (συκοφαντέω) the Jews alone, not listing-together (συγκαταλέγω) their nation with the rest, as either having laboured-together (συμφιλοπονέω) with those and been like-minded (ὁμοφρονέω), or having dogmatised (δογματίζω) similar things in many. Worth then to ask him why ever he has believed (πιστεύω) histories (ἱστορία) of barbarians and Greeks about the antiquity (ἀρχαιότης) of those he named, but of this nation alone makes-false (ψευδοποιέω) the histories. For if each set out their own things truth-lovingly (φιλαλήθως), why do we disbelieve (ἀπιστέω) the prophets of the Jews alone? But if Moses and the prophets wrote many things about their own people favouringly (κεχαρισμένως) to their own cause (λόγος), why shall we not say the like about the writers (συγγραφεύς) among the other nations? Or are Egyptians, slandering (κακολογέω) the Jews in their histories, trustworthy (πιστός) about Jews; but Jews saying the same things about Egyptians, recording themselves to have suffered much unjustly (ἀδίκως) and therefore saying them to have been punished (κολάζω) by God, lie (ψεύδομαι)? And not about Egyptians only must this be said; for we shall find an entanglement (ἐπιπλοκή) of Assyrians with Jews, and these things recorded in the Assyrians' ancient-histories (ἀρχαιολογία). So too the writers of the Jews recorded the Assyrians as enemies (πολέμιος) to themselves, lest I seem, presupposing (προλαμβάνω), to say 'the prophets'. See then straightway the self-love/partiality (τὸ φίλαυτον) of one believing some nations as wise, condemning (καταγινώσκω) others as wholly senseless (ἀνόητος). For hear Celsus saying that there is an ancient doctrine from above/from the beginning (ἀρχαῖος ἄνωθεν λόγος), about which always both the wisest nations and cities and wise men were engaged (καταγίνομαι περί). And he did not wish to call the Jews a wisest nation even similarly to Egyptians, Assyrians, Indians, Persians, Odrysians, Samothracians, Eleusinians.
pass_b_english: Celsus thinks that many nations share a kinship in this same doctrine, and he names all these nations as having originated such a teaching. Yet I do not know how it is that he slanders the Jews alone, not counting their nation with the rest, as one that either shared their studies and was of one mind with them, or taught much the same on many points. It is fair, then, to ask him why he has believed the histories of barbarians and Greeks about the antiquity of the nations he named, while he makes out the histories of this one nation alone to be false. For if each people set down its own affairs out of love for the truth, why should we distrust the prophets of the Jews alone? But if Moses and the prophets wrote many things about their own affairs to favour their own cause, why shall we not say the same about the writers of the other nations too? Or are the Egyptians to be trusted about the Jews when they speak ill of them in their histories, while the Jews are lying when they say the same things about the Egyptians, recording that they themselves suffered much unjustly and saying that for this reason the Egyptians were punished by God?

Nor is this to be said of the Egyptians alone. For we shall find conflict between the Assyrians and the Jews, and this is recorded in the ancient histories of the Assyrians. In the same way the Jewish writers (so as not to seem to beg the question by saying “the prophets”) recorded that the Assyrians were their enemies. See at once, then, the partiality of a man who believes some nations as wise and condemns others as utterly foolish. For listen to Celsus saying: “There is an ancient doctrine that goes back to the beginning, with which the wisest nations and cities and wise men have always been occupied.” Yet he would not call the Jews one of the wisest nations, not even on a level with the Egyptians, Assyrians, Indians, Persians, Odrysians, Samothracians and Eleusinians.

choices.choice: Staged Greek shows '(??)' inside Μωϋσῆς and its cases (Μω(??)υσῆς, Μω(??)σέως): an encoding artefact for the diaeresis, no textual effect. 'κεχαρισμένως τῷ ἑαυτῶν λόγῳ' taken as 'to favour their own cause' (λόγος = account/case). 'ἵνα μὴ δόξω προλαμβάνων': Origen avoids begging the question by calling the Jewish writers 'writers' (συγγραφεῖς) rather than 'prophets'. Celsus's sentence is introduced by ὅτι with a finite verb (ἔστιν), so it is printed as a direct quotation of Celsus. Bracketed [καὶ] before Αἰγυπτίοις is Koetschau's deletion; not translated. The Jewish record of suffering in Egypt and of God punishing the Egyptians refers in general to the Exodus narrative (Exodus 1–12), and the Assyrian wars to the histories in Kings and the prophets; these are general references to whole narratives, not quotations or verse-level allusions, so no inline citation is given. The Egyptian anti-Jewish histories are probably those of Manetho and others answered by Josephus; Origen names none here.
'Yet somehow he slanders' -> 'Yet I do not know how it is that he slanders' (keeps Origen's first-person οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως)
συμφιλοπονῆσαν καὶ ὁμοφρονῆσαν: 'shared their labours and their thinking' -> 'shared their studies and was of one mind with them'
ψευδοποιεῖ: 'treats as fiction' -> 'makes out ... to be false'
added 'For' for γάρ in 'For if each people'
περὶ τῶν παρὰ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς: 'about their own people' -> 'about their own affairs'
ταὐτά: 'the same sort of thing' -> 'the same things'; ἀδίκως 'suffered much injustice' -> 'suffered much unjustly'
ἐπιπλοκή: 'dealings' -> 'conflict' (matches the enemies that follow); added 'For' for γάρ

συγγραφεῖς: 'historians' with an added gloss -> 'writers' + parenthesis that follows the Greek ('so as not to seem to beg the question by saying "the prophets"'), consistent with 'writers of the other nations'
ὡς σοφοῖς: 'because they are wise' -> 'as wise'
ἔθνος σοφώτατον: 'a very wise nation' -> 'one of the wisest nations' (same superlative as Celsus's τὰ σοφώτατα)
